Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t & =-{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-⟨-6,\,12,\,-15⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-12,\,15⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, applying the scalar multiplication rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{0}\frac{2}{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot ⟨6,\,-12,\,15⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-8,\,10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
